builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Zonotopic Analysis of Quantization Error in Neural Networks
summary: The method replaces symbolic DRA propagation (as in QEBVerif) with zonotope and constrained-zonotope abstract interpretation using a unified round-clamp transformer to bound quantization error in quantized ReLU feed-forward networks. It costs implementation of specialized abstract-interpretation machinery, and its advantages are not uniform: gains shrink or reverse at larger perturbation radii and vary across bitwidths. It can fail to help in production because it verifies error bounds on small benchmark-style networks (ACAS Xu) rather than improving inference speed, memory, or accuracy of deployed models.
rationale: This is a formal verification method for bounding quantization error in small ReLU networks, not a deployment or efficiency technique, so it falls outside the reader's production adoption decisions.
technique: Zonotope abstract interpretation for quantization error verification

claims.statement: The method replaces symbolic DRA propagation (as in QEBVerif) with zonotope and constrained-zonotope abstract interpretation using a unified round-clamp transformer to bound quantization error in quantized ReLU feed-forward networks. It costs implementation of specialized abstract-interpretation machinery, and its advantages are not uniform: gains shrink or reverse at larger perturbation radii and vary across bitwidths. It can fail to help in production because it verifies error bounds on small benchmark-style networks (ACAS Xu) rather than improving inference speed, memory, or accuracy of deployed models.

Constrained zonotope method reduces average error-bound widths by ~70-85% and runtimes by 65-80% versus QEBVerif at small perturbation radii (r=3, r=6); plain zonotope variant gives sound bounds ~300x faster on average, but symbolic DRA is tighter at larger radii.
